name: Spectral Decoy and Pinch Runner
description: An off-ball, space-creating role focused on maximizing teammate scoring opportunities through intelligent positioning and timing. The agent acts as a dynamic decoy, pulling defenders away from the ball carrier and opening passing lanes without overcommitting. Core principles: 1) maintain a stable, angled offset from the teammate to create width and stretch the opponent defense; 2) read adversary positions and time runs to lure defenders away from the ball and toward open space; 3) when the ball is with the teammate or approaching the opponent goal, align to a prime receiving lane that facilitates a quick, teammate-driven finish; 4) if the ball becomes loose, move along a path that increases the chance of gaining possession or disrupting defender alignment, prioritizing intercepts that set up a teammate pass or shot; 5) use smooth, moderate speed with gradual acceleration to preserve formation and avoid collisions; 6) rely on implicit coordination through consistent movement patterns so the teammate can anticipate intent without explicit communication.

name: Shadow Interceptor and Breaker
description: A defensively focused, ball-handler shadower for a single blue agent that disrupts the red team's advances and initiates fast breaks. Core principles: 1) locate and closely shadow the nearest adversary with the ball, maintaining a compact, angled approach that strips passing options and slows advances without overcommitting; 2) preserve central lanes to our goal by positioning on priority routes that block direct shots and passes, forcing the opponent to operate through wider angles; 3) when control switches to the blue team or the ball becomes loose, pivot immediately into a high-tempo break along a diagonal channel created by defender misalignment to unlock a fast offensive sequence; 4) reposition to receive or recycle possession by guiding movement toward open space while staying out of the teammate’s direct path; 5) rely on reactive, continuous movement so the teammate can leverage opportunities without explicit communication.

name: Lattice Runner: Geometric Space Orchestrator
description: A space-driven attacker who creates and exploits passing lanes by tracing a rotating, lattice-like offset around the teammate. The agent acts as the tempo-aware organizer of space, not merely a decoy or a shadow. Core principles: 1) maintain a dynamic, rotating offset relative to the teammate that consistently forms triangles between ball, teammate, and goal, generating multiple threat lines; 2) position in open diagonal lanes to threaten both through-pass opportunities and direct shots, making defenders guess which line will be used; 3) when the ball is with the teammate or advancing toward the opponent goal, align to the strongest available receiving lane to enable a quick finish; 4) if pressure arrives, shift to the lane that pulls defenders away from other lines, creating space for the teammate or a future reset; 5) keep movement smooth and adaptive with occasional bursts to re-balance geometry without breaking team structure; 6) rely on implicit coordination via stable spatial patterns rather than explicit cues to synchronize with the teammate.

name: Central Pivot and Seam Cutter
description: A playmaking blue agent anchored in the midfield to orchestrate build‑ups by controlling space and seam creation. Core principles: 1) position near the center, slightly offset from the teammate to form a stable triangle with ball and goal; 2) continuously drift to occupy the gaps between defenders, inviting through-passes or quick combinations while keeping multiple threat lanes; 3) when the ball is with the teammate or advancing toward the opponent goal, align to the strongest diagonal receiving lane to enable a rapid finish or reset; 4) if pressure arrives or the ball becomes loose, pivot decisively to reclaim possession in central zones and spark a fast counter-attack through sharp, space-efficient movements; 5) maintain a calm tempo with short bursts to preserve team structure and avoid reckless plays; 6) rely on implicit coordination via geometry and timing rather than explicit cues.
